items.title: Add default bundle generator
items.context: Add one generator that emits a basic trust/client bundle by default; the senior tier is an explicit opt-in variant. The output files should be easy to source without extra developer fields.
items.userSees: User sees lattice_authority_trust.env and lattice_staging-client.env created successfully, then can source them without being asked for extra developer fields.

happy.desc: Running the default bundle generator writes lattice_authority_trust.env and lattice_staging-client.env and reports success.

edge.desc: Default generation still works when no extra developer fields are supplied or senior mode is absent.

adversarial.desc: Default generation never emits senior filenames or raw secret contents.

verificationEvidence.note: Basic bundle generator writes lattice_authority_trust.env and lattice_staging-client.env, then round-trips through loadAuthorityConfig and resolveAuthorityCustomerApiKey.
The generated bundle is consumable from a different cwd by buildAuthorityStatus and writeAuthorityTrustProfileBundle.
The default tier uses authorityTrustProfileFileNames("basic") and emits only the basic filenames unless senior is explicitly requested.

items.title: Preserve compatibility
items.context: Keep the new Lattice-prefixed filenames and the legacy authority_trust.env / staging-client.env path working together so current automation does not break.
items.userSees: User sees existing authority_trust.env and staging-client.env workflows still load and behave the same, even after the Lattice-prefixed names are added.

happy.desc: Legacy authority_trust.env and staging-client.env aliases still resolve to the same effective bundle contents.

edge.desc: New Lattice-prefixed files and legacy aliases can coexist without duplicate or conflicting reads.

adversarial.desc: Existing automation sourcing only the legacy names continues to work after the rename.

verificationEvidence.note: The legacy staging-client.env sidecar still loads through authority_trust.env and resolves to the same customer API key path semantics.
The loader still accepts a customer API key path from authority_trust.env, so old automation can keep using the legacy sidecar path.
The generator now emits the Lattice-prefixed filenames by default while the compatibility regression block proves the legacy staging-client.env path still works.

items.title: Enable senior bundle path
items.context: Make the senior tier an explicit opt-in variant that produces the senior filenames while keeping the basic bundle as the default path. No extra developer fields.
items.userSees: User sees the senior opt-in emit lattice_senior_authority_trust.env and lattice_senior_staging-client.env only when explicitly requested.

happy.desc: Explicit senior opt-in writes lattice_senior_authority_trust.env and lattice_senior_staging-client.env.

edge.desc: Leaving senior mode off keeps the basic bundle as the default output.

adversarial.desc: The senior path cannot become the silent default or require extra developer fields.

verificationEvidence.note: Explicit senior opt-in round-trips lattice_senior_authority_trust.env and lattice_senior_staging-client.env through the bundle helper.
Omitting tier keeps the basic bundle as the default path; senior filenames are selected only when the caller asks for them.
authorityTrustProfileFileNames exposes senior filenames only through the explicit senior tier, so the default path cannot silently drift to senior.

items.title: Update docs
items.context: Update authority docs to explain the basic bundle, the senior opt-in variant, and the legacy filename compatibility path without introducing a second protocol.
items.userSees: User sees the docs explain one default bundle, one explicit senior variant, and the legacy alias path in the same flow.

happy.desc: Docs show the default bundle, the senior opt-in variant, and the legacy alias path together.

edge.desc: Examples stay consistent with the actual filenames emitted by the generator.

adversarial.desc: Docs do not reintroduce the old Koala wording or a second protocol.

verificationEvidence.note: README, guide, and the CLI contract docs now explain the generated bundle handoff versus live runner variables.
The authority status smoke asserts the generated-bundle note and keeps missing PROJECT_ID / GATE_ACTOR_* in the live-only path.
The authority client smoke still passes for basic and senior bundle generation, preserving the ordinary developer handoff.
